subject.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard

question: Should `deliveryBestEffort: true` continue to send the parent reply while descendant runs are active, as current main explicitly tests, or should active descendant suppression now override that setting?
rationale: Both alternatives are user-visible delivery semantics for an existing cron setting; source shows the branch reverses current behavior, while the reported stale-state path is not yet proven independently reachable.

options.title: Preserve current active-run behavior
options.body: Restore the existing `!params.deliveryBestEffort` gate on the active-run return and add a reproduction that reaches the later stale-interim guard without changing the synthesized text.

options.title: Adopt universal active-run suppression
options.body: Keep the new unconditional active-run suppression only with an explicit owner decision, updated user-facing contract, and proof for both active and inactive descendant scenarios.

recommendation.title: Preserve current active-run behavior
recommendation.body: Restore the existing `!params.deliveryBestEffort` gate on the active-run return and add a reproduction that reaches the later stale-interim guard without changing the synthesized text.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged descendant-gating work is the clearest history link to the delivery-policy invariant this patch changes.
